title: Declare int, float, and complex variables
description:
Write a function `numeric_type_names(age, height, comp_value)` that returns the type name of each argument as a tuple.

Covers source items 1-3 (declare an age as int, a height as float, and a variable holding a complex number) as one exercise - none has a fixed value to check, so declaring one of each numeric type and reporting its type is what's actually being tested.
hints: type(value).__name__ gives the plain-text name of a value's type - 'int', 'float', or 'complex' here.
Return a tuple of type(age).__name__, type(height).__name__, and type(comp_value).__name__, in that order.
expected_behavior: Returns the type name of each of the three arguments.
solution:
def numeric_type_names(age, height, comp_value):
    return type(age).__name__, type(height).__name__, type(comp_value).__name__
explanation: Python has a dedicated literal syntax for complex numbers (3 + 4j) - it's a numeric type just like int and float, with its own arithmetic rules.
